record.text: The group has reached an agreement to pursue a wooden, customizable case for the device.
The presenters (FIE038 and FIE073) will come up with the prototype design for the remote control and show how it looks by the next meeting.
Risk of splinters when using wood; user hand discomfort or injury if the wood finish is not handled properly.
FIE073 will find out more about what 'advanced chip on print' means before the next meeting.
The buttons will be rubber like they are now, not wood, to preserve the tactile experience.
Cost-related concerns: overall product cost and cost of adding a display are not known.
The marketing manager will find out the cost of the display.
There is concern that competitors are copying or stealing the product concept.
Include a battery-life indicator light that dims as the battery dies.
The project manager will submit to management.
We will stick with the simple design for the time being until the cost of adding the display is known.
MIE085 will develop the marketing strategy.
Incorporate a flip-screen feature on the remote to avoid accidental presses or damage when sat on.
Include audio and tactile feedback on button presses and provide a way to turn off voice control.

gold.text: The industrial designer presented casing, power, communication and chip options, recommending a curved wooden case and an advanced chip with audio components.
The industrial designer reported that manufacturing had eliminated other casing materials and proposed custom wooden cases ordered online.
The user interface designer sketched basic controls, an ergonomic shape and a flip cover, and proposed a battery-life indicator, audio/tactile feedback and voice-control switching.
Marketing emphasized novelty, ease of use and willingness to pay for exciting technology, and proposed an LCD display; its cost and usefulness were not yet established.
The team discussed outsourcing custom-case manufacture in lower-cost countries while paying fair wages. Supplier selection and manufacturing arrangements were left for later.
The project manager directed the designers to keep the simple design for now while Ed established the extra cost of adding a display.
The industrial and user interface designers were assigned a prototype by the next meeting; meanwhile marketing was asked for the display cost and marketing strategy.
The industrial designer and user interface designer will jointly produce a prototype/model for the next meeting.
The marketing expert will find the additional cost of the display and develop a marketing strategy, including the extra sales it could support.
Proceed to a prototype based on the simple control layout and the agreed component concept; the display remains a separate cost-dependent option.
Use an advanced chip and a customizable wooden case, with rubber rather than wooden buttons. The ergonomic layout carries forward the simple-interface direction.
Keep the simple design without committing to an LCD until the extra display cost is known.
Explore outsourcing custom-case manufacture at low cost while paying a fair wage; no manufacturer, contact owner or supply agreement was selected.
The industrial designer reported that manufacturing had eliminated every casing material except wood. The user interface designer questioned wood's durability, quality and suitability for users.
The team lacked a firm cost for the display and could not settle whether its usefulness justified the extra expense.
The industrial designer will clarify the technology behind the advanced chip on print before the next meeting.
The project manager will submit the prototype/design to management after the designers have produced and shown it.
